---
title: "How do I fit a regression line and interpret its slope?"
---

## Question

How do I fit a regression line and interpret its slope?

## Decide which method fits

Choose a predictor and an outcome; check their units, paired rows and shape; fit a linear model and inspect the coefficients and residual assumptions.

## Worked example: cars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("cars")
fit <- ru_apply("linear_regression", d, x="speed", y="dist")
stopifnot(inherits(fit,"lm"),is.finite(coef(fit)[2]))
```

The slope estimates the change in expected stopping distance per additional speed unit within the linear model. Neither fitted association nor a high R-squared proves a causal relationship.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("linear_regression", your_data, x="predictor", y="outcome")
```

When curvature dominates, assess model adequacy instead of interpreting the slope as constant across the whole range.

## Optional Palmer penguins example

```r
if (requireNamespace("palmerpenguins", quietly=TRUE)) {
  birds <- ru_data("penguins")
  ru_apply("linear_regression", birds, x="bill_length_mm", y="body_mass_g")
}
```

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("linear_regression")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
